inheritance_boundary: The Rust port uses half-open UTF-8 byte coordinates; the inspected Python editor uses character coordinates and embeds its history. Rust uses immutable same-case artifact ancestry with full bounded replay. These are explicitly versioned implementation differences, not binary old-state compatibility or full inherited-equivalence evidence. Frozen Python tests were not run or modified.
source_snapshot_method: SHA-256 of compact JSON file inventory in code-snapshot.json, including the new text_editing.rs module.
actual_routes: Normal CLI or shared Engine input -> input::seal/structured_intent -> Intent::ImportText -> text_editing::import_explicit_text -> ImportedText -> Core authorized artifact/content/render.

Normal CLI or shared Engine input -> input::seal/structured_intent -> Intent::EditText -> Core actor/case-scoped Store::get_bytes -> text_editing::edit_explicit_text -> bounded exact source/ancestry replay -> atomic patch -> EditedText -> consumed ancestor hashes in Core compute/content/render -> optional existing exact-grant file writer and observed receipt.
route_contract: Headers are 文章を取り込んで:/：, 文章を編集して:/：, and ASCII-case-insensitive text-import:/text-edit:. A newline is mandatory and the complete raw JSON body is retained without Unicode or line-ending normalization.

Import requires exactly text/protected/max_chars. Protected entries require id/start/end/expected. Edit requires exactly base_artifact/expected_text_sha256/edits. Each edit requires id/start/end/expected/replacement/reason. Complete strict JSON framing, duplicate-key rejection and unknown-field/type checks precede execution.

The base digest identifies a real artifact in the frontend-bound actor and current case. Its bytes are hash-checked and its complete canonical record is regenerated from original import/composition source or verified editing ancestry. An independently hashed forged field is rejected if it does not reproduce. No unverified caller JSON or cross-case blob grants access.

All patches refer to the same pre-edit byte coordinates. Expected original text, UTF-8 boundaries, unique IDs, actual changes and nonoverlap are checked before constructing the output. Insertions use empty expected text; deletions use empty replacement text. Equal starting positions are ambiguous. Protected text rejects overlapping edits and interior insertions; boundary insertions preserve text and shift its byte ranges.

Composition quote/condition/caveat protection and explicit imported locks are inherited. Changed text points to the actual replacement string token in the current JSON request. Unchanged text points to its immediate parent artifact range; that artifact retains the earlier origins. No old provenance is silently assigned to replacement text.

The output includes source/output SHA-256, exact original request body, base/output identities, actual consumed ancestor hashes, editing revision, all changes/reasons, protection and continuous output spans. Core stores the artifact and emits exact text with USER_PREMISE guarantee.

The artifact byte budget is checked against the current request before persistence. Current requests exercise existing exact-target file permission/receipt handling. No new external effect, host runner, external neural model or dependency is introduced.

observed_checks: Actual composition output is consumed directly by an edit; quote and condition ranges remain protected. Actual revision-1 output becomes revision-2 input with both parent and root digests retained.

Each current report span, JSON string origin, parent-text slice, source/output digest, request document and consumed artifact link was reread from saved input/result/blob records. The read-only collector independently reconstructs editing output using the recorded original coordinates and replacement text.

Two language-header cases each produced one confirmed 38-byte file with SHA-256 9f34061413c1b8d3a3fd8151d4d476f91392e75633d617110d24f06c4bf504d5. Exact retries preserved the saved result, file modification time and one action identity per store.

Negative CLI cases preserve their original requests and typed SUSPEND records with no result dependencies. They cover late expected-text mismatch after a valid patch, overlap, protected interior insertion/quote change, invalid UTF-8 range, no-op, oversized output, stale text digest, missing/cross-case base, unknown fields, duplicate keys, trailing data, evidence/action/deadline budgets.

Component cases additionally reject rehashed forged report fields/extra fields, unknown artifact types and digest-mismatched loader bytes; enforce the 16-revision history boundary; stop an already expired request before any loader call.
